facts.raw_span: A 20-year-old man
no significant medical history
a 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
the lesion had been present since birth
had not changed in size or character
Vital signs were within normal limits
An MRI of the tongue showed a 1.5-cm protuberant mass
the lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal
demonstrated mild contrast enhancement
had intact overlying mucosa
showed no involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
The sublingual space and major salivary glands appeared normal

concepts.why: The lesion's presence since birth, exophytic and smooth appearance, and partly fatty composition on MRI are consistent with a congenital granular cell tumor.
The midline location and partly fatty appearance of the lesion on MRI, combined with its presence since birth, suggest a lingual thyroid.
The lesion's smooth and regular appearance, combined with its partly fatty composition on MRI and presence since birth, are consistent with a dermoid cyst.
The lesion's partly fatty composition on MRI, combined with its smooth and regular appearance, suggest a lipoma.
The lesion's exophytic and smooth appearance, combined with its partly fatty composition on MRI, are consistent with a hamartoma.
The lesion's presence since birth, combined with its partly fatty composition on MRI, suggest a teratoma.
The lesion's smooth and regular appearance, combined with its mild contrast enhancement on MRI, suggest a hemangioma.
The lesion's smooth and regular appearance, combined with its partly fatty composition on MRI, are consistent with a lymphangioma.

rationales.F03: The presence of a smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue is more typical of Congenital Granular Cell Tumor and Hamartoma.
rationales.F04: The lesion being present since birth is highly suggestive of Congenital Granular Cell Tumor.
rationales.F07: The MRI findings of a protuberant mass are consistent with several diagnoses, but the partly fatty appearance is more suggestive of Lipoma.
rationales.F08: The partly fatty appearance of the lesion is more typical of Lipoma.
